glossary.definition: An immutable package of layered filesystem content plus runtime configuration.
An isolated process (or group) created from an image, with its own namespaces and cgroups.
A filesystem diff in an image. Layers are content-addressed and shared.
The per-container layer that records runtime changes. Deleted with the container.
A service that stores and distributes image manifests and layers.
A mutable human-readable pointer to an image digest.
The immutable content hash identifying an image manifest.
A text recipe of instructions used to build an image.
The files sent to the builder; filtered by .dockerignore.
The modern build engine that executes a DAG of build operations with advanced caching.
A Docker CLI plugin for extended BuildKit builds, including multi-platform output.
A Dockerfile with several FROM stages where only the final stage ships.
A BuildKit mount that persists a directory across builds without adding it to the image.
A tool and specification for defining and running multi-container applications.
The Compose isolation unit; resource names are prefixed with the project name.
A Compose definition of a container, its image/build, configuration and dependencies.
An opt-in group of Compose services enabled with --profile.
A sensitive value mounted at runtime, not baked into an image.
A non-secret configuration file mounted at runtime.
A command that determines whether a container is healthy, distinct from running.
A rule controlling whether Docker restarts a container after exit.
A Linux feature that gives a process a private view of a system resource.
A Linux feature that accounts for and limits resource usage.
The first process in a container; its exit terminates the container.
The kernel terminating a process that exceeded a memory limit; usually exit 137.
Docker-managed persistent storage that outlives containers.
A direct mapping of a host path into a container.
A memory-backed filesystem that disappears when the container stops.
The default single-host network driver; user-defined bridges provide DNS.
A multi-host network driver used by Swarm.
Docker’s name resolution service at 127.0.0.11 on user-defined networks.
The executable a container runs; runtime arguments are appended to it.
Default arguments or command for a container, replaceable at docker run.
The starting filesystem for a Dockerfile stage.
A minimal image containing an application and runtime but no package manager or shell.
Running the Docker daemon as a non-root user to reduce privilege.
A software bill of materials listing components and versions in an image.
Attestation describing how and from what an image was built.
Open Container Initiative, the standards body for image and runtime formats.
A practice of replacing artifacts rather than mutating running systems.
Releasing a new version without dropping user requests.
